column1: # The one declaration of the languages and interpreter versions Blastit ships
# (`MB.67`, `MB.75`). Everything else derives from this file:
#   packaging/languages.sh    the bash loader (sourced by package-set.sh/builders)
#   scripts/languages.py      the Python loader (stdlib only, `uv run --no-project`)
#   scripts/rpm/blastit.spec  generated from this file by `scripts/rpm/gen_spec.py`;
#                             `gen_spec.py --check` (run by `platform_matrix --check`)
#                             fails when the committed spec is stale
#   packaging/package-set.sh  derives its rows here (the core plus one per line) and
#                             asserts only this file's consistency, never a copy
# Six tab-separated fields, one header line, `#` comments. A row is a shim
# package: the package is `blastit-<language>-<version>`, the shim it ships is
# `libblastit_<slug>-<arch>-<libc>.so`, and the two runtime columns are the
# `Recommends:` value (never `Depends:`/`Requires:`). The interpreter-free core
# package `blastit` is not a row: it is the row-less base, spelled `(none)`.
# The sixth field, `channels`, is the release channel(s) a row ships in: a
# space-separated subset of `stable nightly`, in that order (so `stable`,
# `nightly` or `stable nightly`; never empty, never repeated, never reordered).
# The distinction is not cosmetic:
#   * the Rust runtime accepts **every** row, whatever its channels: the same
#     `blastit` binary serves a stable and a nightly install, so its generated
#     tables (`SUPPORTED_*`, `NEWEST_*`, the per-minor constants) cover all rows
#     and a nightly-only minor is selectable on any build;
#   * packaging, the generated RPM spec, the docs tables and the installer's
#     mapping are rendered per channel, so a stable release ships only the
#     `stable` rows and never advertises a nightly-only package.
# Order is the file's order. A version is a string compared per component, never
# a float: `8.10` sorts after `8.9`.
